title: VPC RouteGuard Terraform module: subnet egress health, NAT/IGW failover and endpoint routing
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (vpc-routeguard) that manages subnet routing, NAT/IGW provisioning, VPC Endpoint bindings and automated egress health checks for Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is to prevent silent egress blackholes during upgrades and scale events, enable automatic failover between NAT gateways and reserved egress tiers, and provide clear telemetry and remediation hooks for Console/ops. This module must be importable as a registry-style module and be compatible with both Hosted Private and On-Prem profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for subnet roles, egress_tier (shared|reserved|burst), and preferred_egress (nat|igw|egress-only)
Automated synthetic egress probes run per-subnet and report a health status to a Terraform-managed CloudWatch/Stackdriver telemetry resource (or stable noop for on-prem)
Route table reconciliation ensures no dangling routes to deleted NATs; module avoids route churn during controlled upgrades (use create_before_destroy where needed)
Failover policy: when primary NAT shows degraded probe results, route table updates atomically switch to standby NAT in same AZ, with fallback to cross-AZ reserved pool if local capacity exhausted
VPC Endpoints are created with endpoint policies and explicit route table associations for subnets that opt-in; endpoints are validated by connectivity probes
Module provides output variables for routing map, active_nat_ids, endpoint_ids, and a human-readable egress health summary
Module includes unit/integration test harness (terratest) and CI job that runs on PRs with a mocked cloud environment
Documentation + upgrade notes and plan for migrating existing stacks to module without downtime
implementation_notes: Design as a thin orchestration layer: resource modules for nat_gw, igw, route_tables, and vpc_endpoints with a top-level router that wires them together
Use lifecycle = { create_before_destroy = true } on NAT resources where safe, but avoid it on large public IGW changes that require coordination
Synthetic probes implemented as small lambda / cloud-fn that attempts egress to 3 deterministic endpoints (DNS, S3 HEAD, health-check URL) and records latency+success
Probes emit standardized tags (redwood:module=vpc-routeguard, redwood:stack=<stack>) for Console ingestion
Provide optional on-prem probe shim that writes results to a local metrics collector instead of cloud telemetry
Expose a 'canary' mode that will only update route tables for a percentage of subnets on apply, useful for gradual rollouts
Design outputs such that Console rollout engine can query active_nat_ids and their probe status for visualizing degradations
Consider IPv6 egress case: include egress-only-igw option and treat probe logic accordingly
migration_plan: Phase 1: land module with feature-flagged integration in non-prod stacks. Phase 2: run in shadow mode (create resources but do not change existing route tables) for 2 weeks. Phase 3: enable canary route updates for 10% of subnets, monitor probes and error budgets. Phase 4: full switch with automated rollback on probe regressions or SLO breaches.
work_log: 2025-02-11: Initial RFC drafted and shared in #infra-private. Feedback from SE team: require endpoint policy templates.
2025-02-13: Spike completed for synthetic probe lambda; prototype reports to CloudWatch. Latency stable ~40ms across test VPC.
2025-02-17: Iterated on route reconciliation logic to avoid flapping when NATs are replaced during autoscale. Avoided dependent race by computing desired_state map before applying route changes.
2025-02-20: Added terratest skeleton and basic CI job. Integration tests currently run in sandbox only due to cost.
2025-02-22: Security requested an explicit KMS key option for probe artifacts; added as optional input. Marked module for security review.
Next: implement cross-AZ failover path and add canary rollout flag in top-level module interface.
